searchText: i dont think there can ever be equivocation in this case right? since we have already committed to the `ExecutionPayloadHeader`, is it necessary that only the proposer broadcasts this? if the proposer sources a payload from a MEV-relay, it would have to do 2 round trips. One round trip to get the ExecutionPayloadHeader from the relay, pack it into a beacon block and then broadcast it. The next round trip would be to get the ExecutionPayloadEnvelope from the relay, sign it and broadcast it somehow Anyone can modify the Payload part leaving the block hash intact Making the Payload invalid As for the relay: at the very least prysm will not support blind signing what do you mean "not support blind signing" you mean signing any object? Prysm will not support singing a Payload bid that it hasn't produced got it. so i was just putting down my thoughts on how the builder-spec would look like with ePBS here: https://hackmd.io/XUQhAwAKRhi3vo4yFq13EQ?view things maybe incorrect That post has a ton of statements by which I disagree completely which post are you referring to? Ah no, it's not the one I had in mind, this is a V2 version Need to look at it lmaoo my bad, i should rename it i was just brainstorming on how the proposer<>mev relay interactions would look like with epBS I think this is false: > Builders have strong incentives to route their bids through off-chain relays rather than the enshrined system. Builders have strong incentives to keep their bids secret and opening their own endpoint becoming a relay got it, these are just high level thoughts for now I think we will not have an in protocol API with blind signing anymore. The builder API will be exactly like today except: 1) we will request signed objects 2) we may need to sign the request themselves got it. i think we could probably raise it in the breakout room on friday Sure, just add it to the agenda please?

excerpts.content: if the proposer sources a payload from a MEV-relay, it would have to do 2 round trips. One round trip to get the ExecutionPayloadHeader from the relay, pack it into a beacon block and then broadcast it. The next round trip would be to get the ExecutionPayloadEnvelope from the relay, sign it and broadcast it somehow
